title: Hearing Whiteman live and the fuller orchestral sound
summary: He heard Whiteman at Wilkes-Barre, praised Ross Gorman on Rhapsody in Blue, and relates fuller bands to better phonographs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Did you get a chance at that time to hear bands in person who you had heard on record and you could tell the difference.
Mostly the local bands, traveling bands.
You didn't get to hear any of the --

I got to hear Whiteman later on, I think. I heard him play a concert at the Masonic Hall in Wilkes Barre and went up with our former piano player, Diffy who lived up near there. We got together, we went in and we heard him do -- Morton Downey was even with him then, because that was later. They did the Rhapsody, we wanted to hear the Rhapsody. Ross Gorman, he played it and I still think he plays it -- he understands it. It was written, it's like it was written for him. And I think he does it better than a lot of the guys who do it today.

Simply because there probably may be better clarinet players, if you know what I mean. They have a better conception of things and the Rhapsody to them isn't anything. You know, as a title and as a song, as an era, it was great but it took
a band of that era to play it too.
Because that's where it came from.

Right. So we went up and heard that and by that time, Whiteman's got a full orchestra. He had a fellow by the name of Don Clark came in the band. I think they had three, maybe four saxophones, but they certainly had four brass, two trumpets and two trombones.

And to make my point, everything was getting fuller. And we come into the ortho-phononic stage a little later of the victrolas to where you could hear the bass, where you could hear the guts of the band, which was important and I found myself leaning towards that, so in my senior year, I had three saxophones and three brass and a bass, and the kids used to scream a little bit at the price but it was never -- we made about five or six bucks and I put in a couple of extra bucks for I was the leader.
